title: Minimum Number of Taps to Water a Garden
description: There is a one-dimensional garden on the x-axis. The garden starts at 0 and ends at `n`. There are `n + 1` taps located at points `[0, 1, ..., n]`. Given integer array `ranges` where `ranges[i]` means tap `i` can water `[i - ranges[i], i + ranges[i]]`. Return minimum taps to water whole garden, or -1.
input_format: First line contains `n`. Second line contains `n + 1` range integers.
hints: Convert taps into intervals [max(0, i - r), min(n, i + r)].
For each left boundary, compute the furthest right boundary reachable.
Apply Jump Game II greedy logic to count intervals required to cover [0, n].

reference_solution:
import sys
data = sys.stdin.read().split()
if data:
    n = int(data[0])
    ranges = [int(x) for x in data[1:2+n]]
    max_range = [0] * (n + 1)
    for i, r in enumerate(ranges):
        left = max(0, i - r)
        right = min(n, i + r)
        max_range[left] = max(max_range[left], right)
    taps = cur_end = next_end = 0
    for i in range(n):
        next_end = max(next_end, max_range[i])
        if i == cur_end:
            if next_end <= cur_end: print(-1); sys.exit(0)
            taps += 1
            cur_end = next_end
    print(taps)
